Constitutive models¶

The material registry supports prescribed rigid motion, hyperelastic solids, rate-form plastic solids, Newtonian/Bingham fluids, and local granular flow. Select parameters and units using material selection. These equations describe the default mechanics='updated' configuration.

All tensors are 3 by 3, including the out-of-plane normal stress in plane strain. Cauchy stress is tension positive. Below, p = -tr(stress)/3 is compression positive, s = stress + p I, q = sqrt(3/2 s:s), and the engineering equivalent shear rate is gamma = sqrt(2 D':D'), with D' = dev(dstrain)/dt. Particles.p and .q compute these invariants from current stress. The existing .pressure diagnostic remains tension positive; for Bingham it stores the elastic mean part, excluding instantaneous bulk-viscous stress.

Model parameters¶

Law

Parameters (SI units)

Behaviour

rigid

Optional initial_v

Prescribed planar motion; no constitutive integration.

elastic

K, G > 0 (Pa)

Compressible neo-Hookean elasticity with reference prestress; see deformation and stress.

von_mises

K, G > 0, yield_stress > 0 (Pa), or k with yield_stress=sqrt(3)*k

Perfect J2 plasticity with objective spin integration.

viscous

K, mu_s, mu_v >= 0

Newtonian deviatoric stress 2 mu_s D', bulk viscous stress mu_v tr(D) I, elastic mean-stress increment K tr(dstrain).

pouliquen

K >= 0, rho_s, I_0, eta_max > 0, mu_0, delta_mu >= 0

Bounded friction mu(I)=mu_0+delta_mu I/(I_0+I) and capped viscosity mu p/gamma; mean grain diameter sets I.

bingham

K >= 0 (Pa), mu_s >= 0, mu_0 > mu_s, optional mu_v >= 0 (Pa s), tau_0 >= 0 (Pa)

Continuous bi-viscosity regularisation with engineering shear invariant and dissipative bulk viscosity.

dp

K, G > 0 (Pa), mu > 0, 0 <= beta <= mu

Cohesionless, perfectly plastic Drucker–Prager solid with nonassociated dilation and a zero mean-tensile-strength cutoff. Uses a cone/apex return map.

dp_rate

Same as dp, plus t_star >= 0 (s)

Linear Perzyna overstress regularisation, integrated by backward Euler.

linear_mu

K >= 0 (Pa), mu_0, b >= 0, rho_s > 0 (kg/m³), eta_max > 0 (Pa s), grain sizes and particle compositions

Dense flowing mu(I) = mu_0 + b I, finite viscosity cap, updated compression-positive confinement, explicit zero-pressure/rate limits.

Initialization rejects missing, nonfinite, nonscalar, and inadmissible parameters for these laws. beta is a plastic-potential slope, not an angle. mu in DP is the q/p slope, not tan(friction angle) or the tau/p friction coefficient used by granular flow laws. No Mohr–Coulomb fitting convention is assumed.

Bingham¶

The shear stress is s = 2 eta D', where

eta = min(mu_0, mu_s + tau_0/gamma)
gamma_c = tau_0/(mu_0-mu_s)

At zero rate, eta = mu_0. At tau_0 = 0, the law reduces to a Newtonian fluid with viscosity mu_s, including at zero rate; mu_0 >= mu_s then suffices. An optional gamma_c input must agree with the derived transition. For simple shear the stress is continuous and becomes abs(stress_xy) = tau_0 + mu_s*abs(du/dy) above that transition. This finite-viscosity approximation permits small creep below yield; it does not represent an exactly rigid plug. The engineering shear invariant and the underlying Bingham relation are also described in the FEBio fluid material documentation.

The elastic mean stress increment is K tr(dstrain), and the instantaneous bulk viscous stress is mu_v tr(D) I. The bulk-viscous contribution dissipates mu_v tr(D)^2 per unit current volume.

Drucker–Prager and its rate regularisation¶

The yield function and plastic potential are

f = q - mu*p
g = q - beta*p

For the elastic trial state, the plastic multiplier on the cone is

dlambda = max(f_trial, 0)/(3*G + K*mu*beta + eta_p/dt)
q_new = q_trial - 3*G*dlambda
p_new = p_trial + K*beta*dlambda

eta_p = 0 for dp, and eta_p = 3*G*t_star for dp_rate. Thus the rate model satisfies dlambda/dt = max(f_new, 0)/eta_p on an active surface. t_star is the shear-overstress relaxation time for zero dilation. t_star = 0 gives the rate-independent update exactly. Loading below yield and elastic unloading do not produce plastic flow. Plastic work on the cone is (q - beta*p)*dlambda >= 0 within the admitted parameter range. The use of pressure-dependent yield/flow potentials and a Perzyna flow rule follows standard viscoplasticity; see the Sandia LAMÉ theory. This implementation is the simple linear, perfectly plastic case, without that manual’s additional damage, hardening, or viscoelastic mechanisms.

The mean-tension cutoff is solved together with shear return: if the cone-only candidate has p < 0, impose p = 0 and use dlambda = q_trial/(3*G + eta_p/dt). The rate-independent case reaches the cone apex (p=q=0) without division by either invariant. The rate model can carry finite, dissipative viscous shear overstress at zero confinement; it cannot carry positive mean tension. This is a mean-stress cutoff, not a maximum-principal- stress criterion. The cone return, tension surface, and apex require separate handling, as explained in Itasca’s Drucker–Prager formulation (which uses a different shear-invariant normalisation).

Both solids use a symmetric spin split: rotate the incoming stress by half the incremental spin, perform the constitutive update, then rotate by the other half. This is a corotational hypoelastic integration, exact for pure rigid spin with constant angular velocity. It is not a finite-strain hyperelastic or multiplicative plasticity model.

Linear friction¶

I = gamma * (phi @ grain_sizes) * sqrt(rho_s/p)
eta = min(eta_max, mu_0*p/gamma + b*(phi @ grain_sizes)*sqrt(rho_s*p))
s = 2 eta D'

The sum for eta is evaluated directly so p=0 and gamma=0 do not cause singular arithmetic. At p=0, stress and effective viscosity are zero and the undefined I diagnostic is recorded as zero (mu then records mu_0). At zero rate and positive confinement the effective viscosity is capped, unless mu_0=0, where the finite Newtonian limit of the second term is retained. eta and eta_limited both report the actual effective viscosity. Pressure evolves by K tr(dstrain) and is clamped to compression before computing friction. There is no arbitrary density threshold. Setting b=0 gives a capped constant-friction flowing law.

This is a dense-flow approximation. Its friction grows without bound at high I; it is not a dilute/collisional model or a claim of well-posedness over every flow regime. Local granular rheology has known continuum limitations; see Barker et al.’s stability analysis. Bingham and linear-friction fluids prescribe current stress directly, so the spin correction is not applied to their algebraic viscous stress.

Model limits and unsupported names¶

The plastic laws use corotational hypoelasticity, not multiplicative finite- strain plasticity. Their quadratic stored-energy diagnostic is an estimate. Granular flow laws describe dense flow and need calibration for the material and loading regime. Viscosity caps regularise the calculation and permit creep; they do not impose an exactly rigid plug or prove continuum well-posedness.

elastic_time, ken_kamrin, and ken_simple are unsupported registry names. Use elastic for constant stiffness, pouliquen for the supported bounded local friction law, or linear_mu with b=0 for capped constant friction. These are model choices requiring appropriate parameters, not automatic substitutions. viscous_size and the separate P.F compressible-fluid path are unimplemented.

mechanics='legacy' is a compatibility option with fixed particle volume, occupancy-based density, and incremental constitutive equations. Use the default configuration and the equations on this page for physical interpretation.

Checks and outputs¶

tests/test_constitutive.py covers analytical shear/volume responses, transition continuity, flow reversal, dissipation, unloading, plastic flow direction, yield consistency, cone apex, zero confinement, Perzyna relaxation and timestep convergence, tensor rotation covariance, rigid-spin integration, empty batches, and parameter rejection. The verification guide covers full-solver equilibrium, translation and finite-strain manufactured solutions. Implementation verification does not replace experimental calibration.

The DP loading inputs save data/pq_history.npz and pq_history.png through the standard output callbacks. Tensor stresses use tension-positive signs; plotted p is compression positive. See outputs for file conventions.

poly-mpm

2D material point method with grain-size segregation
